41: function _M:project(t, x, y, damtype, dam, particles)
42: 	if type(particles) ~= "table" then particles = nil end
43: 
44: 	self:check("on_project_init", t, x, y, damtype, dam, particles)
45:

47: 	if game.level.map:checkAllEntities(x, y, "on_project_acquire", self, t, x, y, damtype, dam, particles, false, mods) then
48: 		if mods.x then x = mods.x end
49: 		if mods.y then y = mods.y end
50: 	end
51: 
52: --	if type(dam) == "number" and dam < 0 then return end
53: 	local typ = Target:getType(t)
54: 	typ.source_actor = self
55: 	typ.start_x = typ.start_x or typ.x or (typ.source_actor and typ.source_actor.x or self.x)
56: 	typ.start_y = typ.start_y or typ.y or (typ.source_actor and typ.source_actor.y or self.y)
57: 
58: 	local grids = {}

60: 		if typ.filter and not typ.filter(x, y) then return end
61: 		if not grids[x] then grids[x] = {} end
62: 		grids[x][y] = true
63: 	end
64: 
65: 	-- Stop at range or on block
66: 	local stop_x, stop_y = typ.start_x, typ.start_y
67: 	local stop_radius_x, stop_radius_y = typ.start_x, typ.start_y
68: 	local l, is_corner_blocked

70: 		l = typ.source_actor:lineFOV(x, y, nil, nil, typ.start_x, typ.start_y)
71: 	else
72: 		l = core.fov.line(typ.start_x, typ.start_y, x, y)
73: 	end

75: 		or function(_, bx, by) return false end

7130: function _M:burnArcaneResources(damage)
7131: 	local mana = math.min(self:getMana(), damage)
7132: 	local vim = math.min(self:getVim(), damage/2)
7133: 	local pos = math.min(self:getPositive(), damage/4)
7134: 	local neg = math.min(self:getNegative(), damage/4)
7135: 	self:incMana(-mana)
7136: 	self:incVim(-vim)
7137: 	self:incPositive(-pos)
7138: 	self:incNegative(-neg)
7139: 
7140: 	return math.max(mana, vim * 2, pos * 4, neg * 4)
7141: end

2643: 	-- Art staves may define new flavors or redefine meaning of existing ones; "true" means standard, otherwise it should be a list of damage types.
2644: 	local old_flavor = self:getStaffFlavor(self.flavor_name)
2645: 	local new_flavor = self:getStaffFlavor(flavor)

2647: 	local staff_power = self.combat.staff_power or self.combat.dam
2648: 	local is_greater = self.combat.is_greater
2649: 	for k, v in pairs(staff_command(self)) do
2650: 		if v then

2652: 				local power = staff_power * (v.mult or 1) + v.add

2654: 			elseif type(v) == "number" then  -- shortcut for previous case

179: 			local target = game.level.map(px, py, Map.ACTOR)
180: 			if not target then return end
181: 
182: 			local todel = {}

188: 					elseif e.status == "beneficial" then

199: 	type = "mental",
200: 	subtype = { corruption=true },
201: 	parameters = { power=-3, max_stacks = 8, max_distance = 5, slow_power = 0, stacks = 1  },
202: 	on_gain = function(self, err) return _t"#Target# begins to fear you." end,
203: 	on_lose = function(self, err) return _t"#Target#'s shakes the fear off." end,
204: 	charges = function(self, eff) return eff.stacks or 1 end,
205: 	activate = function(self, eff)
206: 		eff.stack1 = self:addTemporaryValue("numbed", eff.power*eff.stacks)
207: 		if eff.slow_power ~= 0 then eff.stack2 = self:addTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", eff.slow_power*eff.stacks) end
208: 		
209: 		if eff.stacks >= eff.max_stacks then
210: 			eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("wildfire", 1))
211: 		else
212: 			eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("darkness_shield", 1))
213: 		end
214: 		
215: 	end,
216: 	on_merge = function(self, old_eff, new_eff)
217: 		old_eff.dur = new_eff.dur
218: 		
219: 		local stackCount = old_eff.stacks + new_eff.stacks
220: 		if stackCount >= old_eff.max_stacks then 
221: 			stackCount = old_eff.max_stacks
222: 			if old_eff.particle then self:removeParticles(old_eff.particle) end
223: 			old_eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("wildfire", 1))
224: 		end
225: 		
226: 		self:removeTemporaryValue("numbed", old_eff.stack1)
227: 		if old_eff.stack2 then self:removeTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", old_eff.stack2) end
228: 		old_eff.stack2 = nil
229: 		old_eff.stack1 = self:addTemporaryValue("numbed", old_eff.power*stackCount)
230: 		if old_eff.slow_power ~= 0 then old_eff.stack2 = self:addTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", old_eff.slow_power*stackCount) end
231: 		
232: 		old_eff.stacks = stackCount
233: 		
234: 		return old_eff
235: 		
236: 	end,
237: 	deactivate = function(self, eff)		
238: 		self:removeTemporaryValue("numbed", eff.stack1)
239: 		if eff.stack2 then self:removeTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", eff.stack2) end
240: 		if eff.particle then self:removeParticles(eff.particle) end
241: 		
242: 	end,
243: 	on_timeout = function(self, eff)
244: 		if not self.x or not eff.src.x then return end
245: 		-- Check for distance to source and reduce duration if greater than max_distance
246: 		local distance = core.fov.distance(self.x, self.y, eff.src.x, eff.src.y)
247: 		if distance > eff.max_distance then
248: 			eff.dur = eff.dur - 1
249: 		end
250: 	end,
251: }

1232: function _M:combatDefenseBase(fake)
1233: 	local add = 0
1234: 	local light_armor = self:hasLightArmor()
1235: 	if not self:attr("encased_in_ice") then
1236: 		if self:hasDualWeapon() and self:knowTalent(self.T_DUAL_WEAPON_DEFENSE) then
1237: 			add = add + self:callTalent(self.T_DUAL_WEAPON_DEFENSE,"getDefense")
1238: 		end
1239: 		if light_armor and self:knowTalent(self.T_LIGHT_ARMOUR_TRAINING) then
1240: 			add = add + self:callTalent(self.T_LIGHT_ARMOUR_TRAINING,"getDefense")
1241: 		end
1242: 		if not fake then
1243: 			add = add + (self:checkOnDefenseCall("defense") or 0)
1244: 		end
1245: 		if self:knowTalent(self.T_TACTICAL_EXPERT) then
1246: 			local t = self:getTalentFromId(self.T_TACTICAL_EXPERT)
1247: 			add = add + t.do_tact_update(self, t)
1248: 		end
1249: 		if self:knowTalent(self.T_CORRUPTED_SHELL) then
1250: 			add = add + self:getCon() / 3
1251: 		end
1252: 		if self:knowTalent(self.T_STEADY_MIND) then
1253: 			local t = self:getTalentFromId(self.T_STEADY_MIND)
1254: 			add = add + t.getDefense(self, t)
1255: 		end
1256: 		if self:isTalentActive(Talents.T_SURGE) then
1257: 			local t = self:getTalentFromId(self.T_SURGE)
1258: 			add = add + t.getDefenseChange(self, t)
1259: 		end
1260: 		if self:knowTalent(self.T_UMBRAL_AGILITY) then
1261: 			local t = self:getTalentFromId(self.T_UMBRAL_AGILITY)
1262: 			add = add + t.getDefense(self, t)
1263: 		end
1264: 	end
1265: 	local d = math.max(0, self.combat_def + (self:getDex() - 10) * 0.7 + (self:getLck() - 50) * 0.4)
1266: 	local mult = 1
1267: 	if light_armor then
1268: 		if self:knowTalent(self.T_MOBILE_DEFENCE) then
1269: 			mult = mult + self:callTalent(self.T_MOBILE_DEFENCE,"getDef")
1270: 		end
1271: 	end
1272: 
1273: 	return math.max(0, d * mult + add) -- Add bonuses last to avoid compounding defense multipliers from talents
1274: end

1277: function _M:combatDefense(fake, add)
1278: 	if self.combat_precomputed_defense then return self.combat_precomputed_defense end
1279: 	local base_defense = self:combatDefenseBase(true)
1280: 	if not fake then base_defense = self:combatDefenseBase() end
1281: 	local d = math.max(0, base_defense + (add or 0))
1282: 	if self:attr("dazed") then d = d / 2 end
1283: 	return self:rescaleCombatStats(d)
1284: end

1291: 	local d = math.max(0, base_defense + (self.combat_def_ranged or 0) + (add or 0))

738: --- Checks if the talent can be learned
739: -- @param t the talent to check
740: -- @param offset the level offset to check, defaults to 1
741: -- @param ignore_special ignore requirement of special
742: function _M:canLearnTalent(t, offset, ignore_special)
743: 	-- Check prerequisites
744: 	if rawget(t, "require") then
745: 		local req = t.require
746: 		if type(req) == "function" then req = req(self, t) end
747: 		local tlev = self:getTalentLevelRaw(t) + (offset or 1)
748: 
749: 		-- Obviously this requires the ActorStats interface
750: 		if req.stat then
751: 			for s, v in pairs(req.stat) do
752: 				v = util.getval(v, tlev)
753: 				if self:getStat(s) < v then return nil, ("not enough stat: %s"):tformat(s:upper()) end
754: 			end
755: 		end
756: 		if req.level then
757: 			if self.level < util.getval(req.level, tlev) then
758: 				return nil, _t"not enough levels"
759: 			end
760: 		end
761: 		if req.special and not ignore_special then
762: 			if not req.special.fct(self, t, offset) then
763: 				return nil, req.special.desc
764: 			end
765: 		end
766: 		if req.special2 and not ignore_special then
767: 			if not req.special2.fct(self, t, offset) then
768: 				return nil, req.special2.desc
769: 			end
770: 		end
771: 		if req.special3 and not ignore_special then
772: 			if not req.special3.fct(self, t, offset) then
773: 				return nil, req.special3.desc
774: 			end
775: 		end
776: 		if req.talent then
777: 			for _, tid in ipairs(req.talent) do
778: 				if type(tid) == "table" then
779: 					if type(tid[2]) == "boolean" and tid[2] == false then
780: 						if self:knowTalent(tid[1]) then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
781: 					else
782: 						if self:getTalentLevelRaw(tid[1]) < tid[2] then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
783: 					end
784: 				else
785: 					if not self:knowTalent(tid) then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
786: 				end
787: 			end
788: 		end
789: 		if req.birth_descriptors then
790: 			for _, d in ipairs(req.birth_descriptors) do
791: 				if not self.descriptor or self.descriptor[d[1]] ~= d[2] then return nil, ("is not %s"):tformat(_t(d[2])) end
792: 			end
793: 		end
794: 	end
795: 
796: 	if not self:knowTalentType(t.type[1]) and not t.type_no_req then return nil, _t"unknown talent type" end
797: 
798: 	-- Check talent type
799: 	local known = self:numberKnownTalent(t.type[1], t.id, t.type[2])
800: 	if t.type[2] and known < t.type[2] - 1 then
801: 		return nil, _t"not enough talents of this type known"
802: 	end
803: 
804: 	-- Ok!
805: 	return true
806: end

808: --- Formats the requirements as a (multiline) string
809: -- @param t_id the id of the talent to desc
810: -- @param levmod a number (1 should be the smartest) to add to current talent level to display requirements, defaults to 0
811: function _M:getTalentReqDesc(t_id, levmod)
812: 	local t = _M.talents_def[t_id]
813: 	local req = t.require
814: 	if not req then return tstring{}, nil end
815: 	if type(req) == "function" then req = req(self, t) end
816: 
817: 	local tlev = self:getTalentLevelRaw(t_id) + (levmod or 0)
818: 
819: 	local str = tstring{}
820: 
821: 	if not t.type_no_req then
822: 		str:add((self:knowTalentType(t.type[1]) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}), _t"- Talent category known", true)
823: 	end
824: 
825: 	if t.type[2] and t.type[2] > 1 then
826: 		local known = self:numberKnownTalent(t.type[1], t.id, t.type[2])
827: 		local c = (known >= t.type[2] - 1) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
828: 		str:add(c, ("- Lower talents of the same category: %d"):tformat(t.type[2] - 1), true)
829: 	end
830: 
831: 	-- Obviously this requires the ActorStats interface
832: 	if req.stat then
833: 		for s, v in pairs(req.stat) do
834: 			v = util.getval(v, tlev)
835: 			local c = (self:getStat(s) >= v) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
836: 			str:add(c, ("- %s %d"):format(self.stats_def[s].name, v), true)
837: 		end
838: 	end
839: 	if req.level then
840: 		local v = util.getval(req.level, tlev)
841: 		local c = (self.level >= v) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
842: 		str:add(c, ("- Level %d"):tformat(v), true)
843: 	end
844: 	if req.special then
845: 		local c = (req.special.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
846: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special.desc), true)
847: 	end
848: 	if req.special2 then
849: 		local c = (req.special2.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
850: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special2.desc), true)
851: 	end
852: 	if req.special3 then
853: 		local c = (req.special3.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
854: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special3.desc), true)
855: 	end
856: 	if req.talent then
857: 		for _, tid in ipairs(req.talent) do
858: 			if type(tid) == "table" then
859: 				if type(tid[2]) == "boolean" and tid[2] == false then
860: 					local c = (not self:knowTalent(tid[1])) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
861: 					str:add(c, ("- Talent %s (not known)"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid[1]).name), true)
862: 				else
863: 					local c = (self:getTalentLevelRaw(tid[1]) >= tid[2]) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
864: 					str:add(c, ("- Talent %s (%d)"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid[1]).name, tid[2]), true)
865: 				end
866: 			else
867: 				local c = self:knowTalent(tid) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
868: 				str:add(c, ("- Talent %s"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid).name), true)
869: 			end
870: 		end
871: 	end
872: 	if req.birth_descriptors then
873: 		for _, d in ipairs(req.birth_descriptors) do
874: 			local c = self.descriptor and self.descriptor[d[1]] == d[2] and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
875: 			str:add(c, ("- Is %s"):tformat(_t(d[2])), true)
876: 		end
877: 	end
878: 
879: 	return str, req
880: end

822: --- Follow a build order as possible
823: function _M:useBuildOrder()
824: 	local b = self.__use_build_order
825: 
826: 	if self.unused_stats > 0 then
827: 		b.stats.i = b.stats.i or 1
828: 		local nb = 0
829: 
830: 		while self.unused_stats > 0 and nb < #b.stats+1 do
831: 			local stat = b.stats[b.stats.i]
832: 
833: 			if not (self:getStat(stat, nil, nil, true) >= self.level * 1.4 + 20) and
834: 			   not (self:isStatMax(stat) or self:getStat(stat, nil, nil, true) >= 60 + math.max(0, (self.level - 50))) then
835: 				self:incStat(stat, 1)
836: 				self.unused_stats = self.unused_stats - 1
837: 				nb = -1
838: 				game.log("#VIOLET#Following build order %s; increasing %s by 1.", b.name, self.stats_def[stat].name)
839: 			end
840: 			b.stats.i = util.boundWrap(b.stats.i + 1, 1, #b.stats)
841: 			nb = nb + 1
842: 		end
843: 	end
844: 
845: 	if self.unused_talents_types > 0 then
846: 		self.__increased_talent_types = self.__increased_talent_types or {}
847: 
848: 		local learn = true
849: 		while learn do
850: 			learn = false
851: 			for i, tt in ipairs(b.types) do
852: 				if self.unused_talents_types > 0 and (self.__increased_talent_types[tt] or 0) == 0 then
853: 					if not self:knowTalentType(tt) then
854: 						self:learnTalentType(tt)
855: 					else
856: 						self.__increased_talent_types[tt] = (self.__increased_talent_types[tt] or 0) + 1
857: 						self:setTalentTypeMastery(tt, self:getTalentTypeMastery(tt, true) + 0.2)
858: 					end
859: 
860: 					game.log("#VIOLET#Following build order %s; learning talent category %s.", b.name, tt)
861: 					self.unused_talents_types = self.unused_talents_types - 1
862: 					table.remove(b.types, i)
863: 					learn = true
864: 					break
865: 				end
866: 			end
867: 		end
868: 	end
869: 
870: 	if self.unused_talents > 0 then
871: 		local learn = true
872: 		while learn do
873: 			learn = false
874: 			for i, td in ipairs(b.talents) do
875: 				if td.kind == "class" then
876: 					local t = self:getTalentFromId(td.tid)
877: 
878: 					if self.unused_talents > 0 and self:canLearnTalent(t) and self:getTalentLevelRaw(t.id) < t.points then
879: 						self:learnTalent(t.id, true)
880: 						game.log("#VIOLET#Following build order %s; learning talent %s.", b.name, t.name)
881: 						self.unused_talents = self.unused_talents - 1
882: 						table.remove(b.talents, i)
883: 						learn = true
884: 						break
885: 					end
886: 				end
887: 			end
888: 		end
889: 	end
890: 
891: 	if self.unused_generics > 0 then
892: 		local learn = true
893: 		while learn do
894: 			learn = false
895: 			for i, td in ipairs(b.talents) do
896: 				if td.kind == "generic" then
897: 					local t = self:getTalentFromId(td.tid)
898: 
899: 					if self.unused_generics > 0 and self:canLearnTalent(t) and self:getTalentLevelRaw(t.id) < t.points then
900: 						self:learnTalent(t.id, true)
901: 						game.log("#VIOLET#Following build order %s; learning talent %s.", b.name, t.name)
902: 						self.unused_generics = self.unused_generics - 1
903: 						table.remove(b.talents, i)
904: 						learn = true
905: 						break
906: 					end
907: 				end
908: 			end
909: 		end
910: 	end
911: end

913: function _M:loadBuildOrder(file)
914: 	local f = fs.open("/build-orders/"..file, "r")
915: 	if not f then return end
916: 
917: 	local b = {name="xxx", stats={}, talents={}, types={}}
918: 
919: 	local cur = "name"
920: 	while true do
921: 		local line = f:readLine()
922: 		if not line then break end
923: 		line = line:gsub('[\r\n"]', '')
924: 		local split = line:split(lpeg.S",; \t")
925: 
926: 		if split[1] == "#Name" then cur = "name"
927: 		elseif split[1] == "#Stats" then cur = "stats"
928: 		elseif split[1] == "#Talents" then cur = "talents"
929: 		elseif split[1] == "#Types" then cur = "types"
930: 		else
931: 			if cur == "name" then b.name = table.concat(split, " "):trim()
932: 			elseif cur == "stats" then
933: 				b.stats = {}
934: 				for i, s in ipairs(split) do if s ~= "" then table.insert(b.stats, s) end end
935: 			elseif cur == "talents" then
936: 				table.insert(b.talents, {kind=split[2], tid=split[3]})
937: 			elseif cur == "types" then
938: 				table.insert(b.types, split[2])
939: 			end
940: 		end
941: 	end
942: 
943: 	if #b.stats > 0 and #b.talents > 0 then
944: 		self.__use_build_order = b
945: 	end
946: end

65: 			local blocked = false

70: 					-- blocked

91: function checkMaxSummon(self, silent, div, check_attr)
92: 	div = div or 1
93: 	local nb = 0
94: 
95: 	-- Count party members
96: 	if game.party:hasMember(self) then
97: 		for act, def in pairs(game.party.members) do
98: 			if act.summoner and act.summoner == self and act.wild_gift_summon and not act.wild_gift_summon_ignore_cap and (not check_attr or act:attr(check_attr)) then nb = nb + 1 end
99: 		end
100: 	elseif game.level then
101: 		for _, act in pairs(game.level.entities) do
102: 			if act.summoner and act.summoner == self and act.wild_gift_summon and not act.wild_gift_summon_ignore_cap and (not check_attr or act:attr(check_attr)) then nb = nb + 1 end
103: 		end
104: 	end
105: 
106: 	local max = util.bound(math.floor(self:combatStatScale("cun", 10^.5, 10)),1,math.max(1,math.floor(self:getCun() / 10))) -- scaling slows at higher levels of cunning
107: 	if self:attr("nature_summon_max") then
108: 		max = max + self:attr("nature_summon_max")
109: 	end
110: 	max = math.ceil(max / div)
111: 	if nb >= max then
112: 		if not silent then
113: 			game.logPlayer(self, "#PINK#You can manage a maximum of %d summons at any time. You need %d Cunning to increase your limit.", nb, math.max((nb+1)*10, (nb+1)^2))
114: 		end
115: 		return true, nb, max
116: 	else
117: 		return false, nb, max
118: 	end
119: end

141: 	if not game.level then return stats end

149: 			end
150: 			if act.ghoul_minion then stats.nb_ghoul = stats.nb_ghoul + 1 end
151: 			if act.lord_of_skulls then stats.lord_of_skulls = act end
152: 			if act.is_bone_giant then stats.bone_giant = act end
153: 			if act.dread_minion then stats.dread = act end
154: 			stats.list[#stats.list+1] = act
155: 		end end

159: 			if act.skeleton_minion then

161: 				if act.skeleton_minion == "mage" then stats.has_skeleton_mage = true end

160: --- Generate targeting parameters for summoning talents
161: -- Only used by the (tactical) AI to test tactical parameters vs. aitarget when evaluating talents
162: function SummonTarget(self, t)

166: -- returns grid coords in which to place a summon (if self.__talent_running is set, i.e. t.action is being executed)
167: -- or the exact coordinates of an NPC's target
168: -- allows the (tactical) AI to test the talent against aitarget properly
169: function onAIGetTargetSummon(self, t)
170: 	local aitarget = self.ai_target.actor
171: 	if aitarget and self:reactionToward(aitarget) < 0 then
172: 		if self.__talent_running then -- get coords in which to place the summon
173: --print("[onAIGetTargetSummon] placing summon", t.id) -- debugging
174: 			return t.aiSummonGrid(self, t)
175: 		else -- getting aitarget info
176: --print("[onAIGetTargetSummon] getting aitarget info", t.id) -- debugging
177: 			return aitarget.x, aitarget.y, aitarget
178: 		end
179: 	end
180: end
181: 
182: --- find a path between summoner and target (limit to range 25, effective)
183: function summonPath(self)
184: 	local aitarget = self.ai_target.actor
185: 	self.turn_procs.summoning = self.turn_procs.summoning or {}
186: 	if aitarget and self:reactionToward(aitarget) < 0 and core.fov.distance(self.x, self.y, aitarget.x, aitarget.y) <= 25 then
187: 		if config.settings.log_detail_ai > 1 then print(("[summonPath] calculating new summoning path [%d]%s at (%s, %s) to [%d]%s at (%s, %s)"):format( self.uid, self.name, self.x, self.y, aitarget.uid, aitarget.name, aitarget.x, aitarget.y)) end
188: 		local tx, ty = self:aiSeeTargetPos(aitarget)
189: 		local ast = Astar.new(game.level.map, self)
190: 		local path = ast:calc(tx, ty, self.x, self.y, nil, nil,
191: 			function(gx, gy) -- path around other actors
192: 				if gx == self.x and gy == self.y then return true end
193: 				return not game.level.map(gx, gy, engine.Map.ACTOR)
194: 			end
195: 		)
196: 		if path then
197: 			local range = 10
198: 			path[0] = {x=tx, y=ty} -- place origin
199: 			local stoptgtLOS, stopselfLOS = false, false
200: 			for i = 0, #path do
201: 				local node = path[i]
202: 				if not stoptgtLOS then 
203: 					node.tgtLOS = self:hasLOS(node.x, node.y, "block_move", range, tx, ty)
204: 					if node.tgtLOS then path.nearTgtLOS = i else stoptgtLOS = true end
205: 				end
206: 				if not stopselfLOS then 
207: 					node.selfLOS = self:hasLOS(node.x, node.y, "block_move", range)
208: 					if node.selfLOS and not path.farSelfLOS then path.farSelfLOS = i stopselfLOS = true end
209: 				end
210: 			end
211: 			self.turn_procs.summoning.path = path
212: --print("new summoning path:") table.print(path)
213: 			return path
214: 		else
215: 			self.turn_procs.summoning.path = false
216: 		end
217: 	else
218: 		self.turn_procs.summoning.path = false
219: 	end
220: 	if aitarget and config.settings.log_detail_ai > 1 and self.turn_procs.summoning.path == false then print(("[summonPath] no summoning path [%d]%s at (%s, %s) to [%d]%s at (%s, %s)"):format(self.uid, self.name, self.x, self.y, aitarget.uid, aitarget.name, aitarget.x, aitarget.y)) end
221: 	return self.turn_procs.summoning.path
222: end
223: 
224: -- find a reasonable spot for a MELEE summon to be placed
225: -- attempts to place the summon adjacent to the target
226: -- returns x, y coordinates or false if no spot can be found
227: function aiSummonGridMelee(self, t)
228: 	if self.turn_procs.summoning and self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id] then return self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id][1], self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id][2] end
229: 	local path = self.turn_procs.summoning and self.turn_procs.summoning.path
230: 	if path == nil then path = summonPath(self) end
231: --print("[aiSummonGridMelee] path:", path) table.print(path)
232: 	if path then
233: 		local range, max_dist = self:getTalentRange(t), 1
234: 		local node = math.max(path.farSelfLOS, #path - range)
235: 		if config.settings.log_detail_ai > 2 then print(("[aiSummonGridMelee] found melee summon node %d at (%d, %d) max_dist=%s"):format(node, path[node].x, path[node].y, max_dist)) end
236: 		if node > max_dist then return false end
237: 		local tg = self:getTalentTarget(t) or {type="bolt", nowarning=true, nolock=true, talent=t}
238: 		tg.range, pass_terrain = range, false
239: 		local ok, nx, ny
240: 		ok, ok, ok, nx, ny = self:canProject(tg, path[node].x, path[node].y)
241: --print("Projection result:", ok, nx, ny)
242: 		local x, y = util.findFreeGrid(nx, ny, 1, true, {[Map.ACTOR]=true})
243: 		if config.settings.log_detail_ai > 1 then print("[aiSummonGridMelee] Find Free Grid result:", x, y) end
244: 		if not (x and y) or core.fov.distance(path[0].x, path[0].y, x, y) > max_dist then return false end
245: 		self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id] = {nx, ny}
246: 		return nx, ny
247: 	end
248: 	return false
249: end
250: 
251: -- find a reasonable spot for a RANGED summon to be placed
252: -- attempts to place the summon within or close to LOS of the target but slightly off axis so it doesn't block the summoner's attacks
253: -- returns x, y coordinates or false if no spot can be found
254: function aiSummonGridRanged(self, t)
255: 	if self.turn_procs.summoning and self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id] then return self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id][1], self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id][2] end
256: 	local path = self.turn_procs.summoning and self.turn_procs.summoning.path
257: 	if path == nil then path = summonPath(self) end
258: 	if path then
259: 		local range, max_dist = self:getTalentRange(t), math.min(5, t.on_arrival and self:isTalentActive(self.T_MASTER_SUMMONER) and self:knowTalent(self.T_GRAND_ARRIVAL) and self:callTalent(self.T_GRAND_ARRIVAL, "radius") or 5)
260: 		local node = math.max(path.farSelfLOS, #path - range) -- closest possible node to target
261: 		if node > max_dist then return false end
262: 		node = math.min(max_dist, math.max(path.nearTgtLOS, path.farSelfLOS))
263: 		local nx, ny = path[node].x, path[node].y
264: 		local tgtDir = util.getDir(path[0].x, path[0].y, self.x, self.y)
265: 		if config.settings.log_detail_ai > 2 then print(("[aiSummonGridRanged] found ranged summon node %d at (%d, %d), dir=%s"):format(node, nx, ny, tgtDir)) end
266: 		-- if possible place the summon to the side of the LOS path to the target
267: 		local sides=util.dirSides(tgtDir, self.x, self.y)
268: 		local allow_grids = {}, sx, sy
269: 		local tg = self:getTalentTarget(t) or {type="bolt", nowarning=true, nolock=true, talent=t}
270: 		tg.range = range
271: 		for s, dir in pairs(sides) do
272: 			sx, sy = util.dirToCoord(dir, nx, ny)
273: 			sx, sy = sx + nx, sy + ny
274: 			if not game.level.map:checkAllEntities(sx, sy, "block_move") and self:hasLOS(sx, sy, "block_move", max_dist, path[0].x, path[0].y) and self:canProject(tg, sx, sy) then
275: 				allow_grids[#allow_grids+1] = {sx, sy}
276: 			end
277: 		end
278: --table.print(allow_grids, "_ag_")
279: 		local grid = rng.table(allow_grids)
280: 		if grid then nx, ny = grid[1], grid[2] end
281: 		self.turn_procs.summoning[t.id] = {nx, ny}
282: 		if config.settings.log_detail_ai > 1 then print(("[aiSummonGridRanged] picked summon grid at (%d, %d)"):format(nx, ny)) end
283: 		return nx, ny
284: 	end
285: 	return false
286: end

288: -- Checks that there is a reasonable spot to place a summon
289: function aiSummonPreUse(self, t, silent, fake)
290: 	if self.ai_target.actor and self:reactionToward(self.ai_target.actor) < 0 then
291: 		if not self.ai_state.target_last_seen or game.turn - (self.ai_state.target_last_seen.GCknown_turn or 0) <=50 then
292: 			return t.aiSummonGrid(self, t)
293: 		end

395: 				local scoreBonus = game.level.arena.bonus * 0.2
396: 				local clearBonus = math.ceil(game.level.arena.currentWave ^ 1.85)
397: 				local rankBonus = math.floor(game.level.arena.rank) * 20
398: 				local expAward = (dangerBonus + scoreBonus + clearBonus + rankBonus) * game.level.arena.bonusMultiplier
399: 				local x, y = game.level.map:getTileToScreen(game.player.x, game.player.y)
400: 				game.player:gainExp(expAward)
401: 				game.player:incMoney(game.level.arena.bonusMultiplier)
402: 				game.level.arena.score = game.level.arena.score + game.level.arena.bonus
403: 				game.flyers:add(x, y, 90, 0, -1, ("Round Clear! +%s EXP!"):tformat(expAward), { 2, 57, 185 }, true)
404: 				game.log("%sWave clear!", col)
405: 				game.log("%sClear bonus: %s%s%s! Score bonus: %s%s%s! Danger bonus: %s%s%s! Rank bonus: %s%s%s!", col, hgh, clearBonus, col, hgh, scoreBonus, col, hgh, dangerBonus, col, hgh, rankBonus, col)
406: 				game.log("%sYour experience increases by %s%d%s!", col, hgh, expAward, col)
407: 				game.log("%sYou earn %s gold for your victory!", col, game.level.arena.bonusMultiplier)
408: 				game.player.changed = true
409: 			end,
410: 
411: 			clearRound = function () --Relax and give rewards.
412: 				--Do rewarding.
413: 				local val = game.level.arena.pinchValue
414: 				local plvl = game.player.level
415: 				game.level.arena.doReward(val)
416: 				--Set rest time.
417: 				local rest_time = val
418: 				if not plvl == game.player.level then --If bonuses made the player level up, give minimal time.
419: 					if rest_time > 30 then rest_time = 30 end
420: 				else
421: 					if rest_time < 25 then rest_time = 25
422: 					elseif rest_time > 80 then rest_time = 80
423: 					end
424: 				end
425: 				game.level.turn_counter = rest_time * 10
426: 				game.level.max_turn_counter = rest_time * 10
427: 				game.level.arena.initWave(rest_time)
428: 			end,
429: 
430: 			checkPinch = function ()
431: 				if game.level.arena.danger > game.level.arena.dangerTop and game.level.arena.pinch == false then --The player is in a pinch!
432: 					if game.level.arena.danger - game.level.arena.dangerTop < 10 then return end --Ignore minimal excess of power.
433: 					game.level.arena.pinch = true
434: 					game.level.arena.pinchValue = game.level.arena.danger - game.level.arena.dangerTop
435: 					game.level.arena.bonus = (game.level.arena.pinchValue * 20) + 200
436: 					game.level.arena.closeGates()
437: 				elseif game.level.arena.danger <= 0 and game.level.arena.pinch == true then --The player cleared the round.
438: 					if game.level.arena.event == 0 then
439: 						game.level.arena.clearRound()
440: 					elseif game.level.arena.lockEvent == false then --Call minibosses or boss next turn.
441: 						game.level.arena.initEvent = true
442: 					else --Round is clear
443: 						game.level.arena.clearRound()
444: 					end
445: 				end
446: 			end,
447: 		}
448: 		local Chat = require "engine.Chat"
449: 		local chat = Chat.new("arena-start", {name=_t"Arena mode"}, game.player, {text = level.arena.printRankings()})

39: 	category = "Forbidden Cults", always_pop = true,
40: 	name = _t"Lessons of Inevitability - Introduction",
41: 	lore = _t[[In the Age of Dusk, it seemed that the world was ending to many of Eyal's inhabitants. The destruction caused by the Spellblaze left the land withered and scorched. Food was scarce, disease was rampant and everyone was desperate. For a select few, their salvation came from an unlikely visitor. An entity they simply came to knew as The Teacher visited Eyal from somewhere beyond the stars, emerging from an ancient Sher'tul farportal. It discovered a group of survivors in the depths of Eyal which begged it for knowledge, anything they could use as a weapon against the horrors ravaging their world.
42: 
43: Out of charity and kindness, it agreed to teach them how to wield the power of entropy itself. However, it made it clear to them that this was not a power to be taken lightly and could very well bring about their doom. As desperate as they were, all of them agreed without a second thought, heedless of the consequences it could have.
44: 
45: Hithre was one of The Teacher's pupils, a Shalore who became one of the first to wield entropic magic in the entirety of Eyal.]],
46: }

106: newLore{
107: 	id = "races-krog",
108: 	category = "races",
109: 	name = _t"Loremaster Greynot's Analysis of the Races - Chapter 12 - Krogs",
110: 	lore = _t[[The krog are perhaps the youngest of the intelligent races of Maj'Eyal, only coming into existence recently. They claim that they were formerly ogres that have had their runes removed, somehow surviving having their runes replaced by a combination of natural infusions and drakes blood. The removal of their runes was orchestrated by the Ziguranth, who apparently decided action needed to be taken to prevent all ogres from being horribly and brutally killed as a result of the Spellhunt, leading to the creation of the krog. The official reasons given by the Ziguranth for this action was that the ogres were unfortunate victims of magic rather then perpetrators of it, and the Ziguranth were just looking to help to free them from the taint of the arcane.
111: 
112: Due to the fact that they were originally ogres, it comes as no surprise that the two races share much with each other. They tend to have similar hair coloring, facial features, and other similar traits. The average krog is a bit shorter then a ogre at 8'2" and perhaps a little leaner, but otherwise the rest of their body dimensions remain the same. One would likely be hard pressed to distinguish a krog from an ogre or vice versa if it wasn't for the heavy tint of greens and browns within their eyes and skin, likely a side effect of whatever natural process the Ziguranth employed to strip them of their runes.
113: 
114: The majority of the krog tend to live in or around the middle of the continent where the heart of Ziguranth territory lies and they have been known to take up arms in service to the anti-magic cause. Indeed one may find that the majority of any Ziguranth Patrol one may encounter is usually made up of krog fighters. All krog seem to demonstrate some connection to nature as well as possessing abilities to combat mages, not to mention harbor a huge hatred towards anyone that deals with magic in any way. Indeed, a krog's disdain for the arcane begs the question if perhaps the Ziguranth did a bit more then just remove the runes from their bodies.
115: 
116: Commonly when they are not in the employ of the Ziguranth, or otherwise answering the call to do battle with a rogue mage, the krog have been known to contract themselves out as laborers to whomever may hire them. Like ogres, krog are also known for having impressive appetites and one can find many krog farmers plowing fields to grow food for themselves to eat. They are also known for their talents in mixing infusions, producing the majority of what one might find in the markets around the continent.
117: 
118: Of course no analysis of the krog would be complete without mentioning the many stories, songs, and artwork that revolve around their many pursuits. A lot of encouragement is directed at younger krogs by their peers to venture out into the world and perform heroic deeds. This course of action seems less to do with valor, glory, or riches; something one might expect of a typical 'adventurer' and more to do with the mistrust that followed them formerly being ogres. In an effort to combat their initial image they had as former ogres, the krog sought to commit themselves to gaining a new image through achievement of impressive feats. To this end they seem to have been rather successful as evidenced by the creation of the many artistic works told about them. ]]}

120: newLore{
121: 	id = "races-drem",
122: 	category = "races",
123: 	name = _t"Loremaster Greynot's Analysis of the Races - Chapter 13 - Drems",
124: 	lore = _t[[Eyal's underground is abundant with strange, and not particularly wholesome, creatures. Many of them are mindless monstrosities, unable to be reasoned with and best left alone. However, perhaps the most unusual of these creatures are the Drem. For the longest time, Drem were presumed to simply be another form of horror which dwelled in Eyal's underground. The recent emergence of thinking Drem, however, has forced many scholars to reassess their race as a whole.
125: 
126: A Drem is roughly the same height as a Dwarf and has a vaguely similar facial structure as well. This is where the similarities between the two races tend to end. Drem have no distinguishing facial features and are incapable of growing beards like dwarves, instead growing wiry and unkempt patches of hair which vary greatly in thickness. Due to the lack of facial features such as eyes, ears, a mouth and a nose, it is not currently known how a Drem eats or how they sense things around them. The mental faculties of thinking Drem seems to vary wildly from each individual as well. Some are barely more capable of rational thought than feral Drem, while others have gained intellect comparable to the brightest minds of Eyal.
127: 
128: As they have only recently come out of their previously mindless states, the Drem are a people who are completely disconnected with the world around them. They possess no cultural identity or history to fall back on and sit on the precipice between the civilised races of Eyal's surface and the horrors of Eyal's underground. Many suspect that they possess some connection to the dwarves, the prevailing theory being that they are some sort of corrupted offshoot of that proud race. There has been little research into the subject and little evidence found to substantiate these claims, however. What impact the Drem will have on Eyal's future can only be speculated upon at this point.]]}

194: function craft_levelup(self, t, lvl, old_lvl, lvl_raw, old_lvl_raw, from_dialog)
195: 	-- hack around 1.4 bug :<
196: 	if self:isClassName("mod.dialogs.LevelupDialog") then self = self.actor end

203: 		   self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_THERAPEUTICS) >= 5 and self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_CHEMISTRY) >= 5 and self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_EXPLOSIVES) >= 5 and 
204: 		   self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_SMITH) >= 5 and self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_MECHANICAL) >= 5 and self:getTalentLevelRaw(self.T_ELECTRICITY) >= 5
205: 		   then

207: 		end
208: 	end)

211: 	-- Learn tinkers
212: 	---------------------------------------------------------------------------
213: 	game.party.tinkers_auto_learnt = game.party.tinkers_auto_learnt or {}
214: 	game.party.tinkers_auto_learnt[t.id] = game.party.tinkers_auto_learnt[t.id] or 0
215: 	if game.party.tinkers_auto_learnt[t.id] >= 2 then return end

217: 	local function learn_one(force_level)
218: 		local tinker_id = nil
219: 		local possibles = {}
220: 		for tid, tinker in pairs(game.party.__tinkers_ings) do if tinker.random_schematic and tinker.talents and tinker.talents[t.id] and not game.party:knowTinker(tinker.id) then
221: 			local max, maxid = -1, ""
222: 			for ttid, lvl in pairs(tinker.talents) do if lvl > max then max = lvl; maxid = ttid end end
223: 			local is_major = maxid == t.id
224: 			if (not force_level or tinker.talents[t.id] == force_level) and is_major then

594: newEffect{
595: 	name = "AWESOME_TOSS", image = "talents/awesome_toss.png",
596: 	desc = _t"Awesome Toss",
597: 	long_desc = function(self, eff) return ("All resistances increased by %d%%, randomly attacks two foes each turn at random."):tformat(eff.resist, eff.dam) end,
598: 	type = "physical",
599: 	cancel_on_level_change = true,
600: 	subtype = { steamtech=true, awesome=true, resistance=true },
601: 	status = "beneficial",
602: 	on_gain = function(self, err) return _t"#Target# tosses steamguns in the air, awesome!", true end,
603: 	on_lose = function(self, err) return _t"#Target# somehow catches the falling steamguns.", true end,
604: 	parameters = {dam=10, resist=10},
605: 	callbackOnActBase = function(self, eff)
606: 		self.disarmed = self.disarmed - 1
607: 		local weapon, ammo, offweapon = self:hasDualArcheryWeapon("steamgun")
608: 		self.disarmed = self.disarmed + 1
609: 		local realweapon = weapon
610: 		weapon = weapon and weapon.combat
611: 		local realoffweapon = offweapon
612: 		offweapon = offweapon and offweapon.combat
613: 		if not weapon or not offweapon then return end
614: 
615: 		self.disarmed = self.disarmed - 1
616: 
617: 		local targets = {main={}, off={}, dual=true}
618: 		local function run(weapon, where)
619: 			local range = weapon.range or 6
620: 			local tgts = {}
621: 			self:project({type="ball", radius=range, start_x=eff.x, start_y=eff.y}, eff.x, eff.y, function(px, py)
622: 				local target = game.level.map(px, py, Map.ACTOR)
623: 				if not target or self:reactionToward(target) >= 0 then return end
624: 				tgts[#tgts+1] = target
625: 			end)
626: 			if #tgts == 0 then return end
627: 
628: 			local target = rng.table(tgts)
629: 			where[#where+1] = {x=target.x, y=target.y, ammo=ammo.combat}
630: 		end
631: 		run(weapon, targets.main)
632: 		run(offweapon, targets.off)
633: 
634: 		if #targets.main > 0 or #targets.off > 0 then
635: 			local sound = weapon.sound
636: 			if sound then game:playSoundNear(self, sound) end
637: 			self:archeryShoot(targets, self:getTalentFromId(self.T_AWESOME_TOSS), {start_x=eff.x, start_y=eff.y}, {mult=eff.dam})
638: 		end
639: 
640: 		self.disarmed = self.disarmed + 1
641: 	end,
642: 	activate = function(self, eff)
643: 		eff.x, eff.y = self.x, self.y
644: 		self:effectTemporaryValue(eff, "resists", {all=eff.resist})
645: 		self:effectTemporaryValue(eff, "disarmed", 1)
646: 	
647: 		eff.p1 = game.level.map:particleEmitter(eff.x, eff.y, 2, "vapour_spin", {radius=1, smoke="particles_images/smoke_whispery_bright"})
648: 		eff.p2 = game.level.map:particleEmitter(eff.x, eff.y, 2, "vapour_spin", {radius=1, smoke="particles_images/smoke_heavy_bright"})
649: 		eff.p3 = game.level.map:particleEmitter(eff.x, eff.y, 2, "vapour_spin", {radius=1, smoke="particles_images/smoke_dark"})
650: 		eff.p4 = game.level.map:particleEmitter(eff.x, eff.y, 2, "steamgun_spin", {})
651: 	end,
652: 	deactivate = function(self, eff)
653: 		if eff.p1 then game.level.map:removeParticleEmitter(eff.p1) end
654: 		if eff.p2 then game.level.map:removeParticleEmitter(eff.p2) end
655: 		if eff.p3 then game.level.map:removeParticleEmitter(eff.p3) end
656: 		if eff.p4 then game.level.map:removeParticleEmitter(eff.p4) end
657: 	end,
658: }

203: 			local fx, fy, grids

206: 			if tactic == "escape" then -- try to jump away

213: 			else -- try to jump to target location

616: --- Re-order inventory, sorting and stacking it
617: -- sort order is type > subtype > name > getNumber()
618: function _M:sortInven(inven)
619: 	if not inven then inven = self.inven[self.INVEN_INVEN] end
620: 	inven = self:getInven(inven)
621: 	if not inven then return end
622: --	local stacked, last, stacklimit = false, false, inven.stack_limit or math.huge
623: 	local stacked, last, stacklimit = false, false, self:invenStackLimit(inven)
624: 
625: 	-- First, stack objects from top
626: 	for i = 1, #inven do
627: 		if not inven[i] then break end
628: 		-- If it is stackable, look for objects after it that can stack into it
629: 		if inven[i]:stackable() then
630: 			for j = #inven, i + 1, -1 do
631: 			-- check stack limit
632: 				stacked, last = inven[i]:stack(inven[j], false, stacklimit - inven[i]:getNumber())
633: 				if stacked then
634: 					if last then
635: 						table.remove(inven, j)
636: 					else
637: 						break
638: 					end
639: 				end
640: 			end
641: 		end
642: 	end
643: 
644: 	-- Sort them
645: 	table.sort(inven, function(a, b)
646: 		local ta, tb = a:getTypeOrder(), b:getTypeOrder()
647: 		local sa, sb = a:getSubtypeOrder(), b:getSubtypeOrder()
648: 		if ta == tb then
649: 			if sa == sb then
650: 				if a.name == b.name then
651: 					return a:getNumber() > b:getNumber()
652: 				else
653: 					return a.name < b.name
654: 				end
655: 			else
656: 				return sa < sb
657: 			end
658: 		else
659: 			return ta < tb
660: 		end
661: 	end)
662: 	self.changed = true
663: end

4547: --- Call when an object is worn
4548: -- This doesnt call the base interface onWear, it copies the code because we need some tricky stuff
4549: function _M:onWear(o, inven_id, bypass_set, silent)
4550: 	o.wielded = {}
4551: 
4552: 	if self.player then o:forAllStack(function(so) so.__transmo = false end) end
4553: 
4554: 	local set_list_list = o.set_list
4555: 	if type(set_list_list) == 'function' then
4556: 		set_list_list = set_list_list(o, self, inven_id)
4557: 	end
4558: 	if set_list_list and not bypass_set then
4559: 		if not set_list_list.multiple then set_list_list = {single = set_list_list} end
4560: 		set_list_list = table.clone(set_list_list)
4561: 		set_list_list.multiple = nil
4562: 		for set_id, set_list in pairs(set_list_list) do
4563: 			local set_objects = {}
4564: 			for _, conditions in ipairs(set_list) do
4565: 				-- Find the object in the inventory.
4566: 				local object, index, object_inven_id
4567: 				if conditions.inven_id then
4568: 					object_inven_id = util.getval(conditions.inven_id, o, self, inven_id)
4569: 					local object_inven = self:getInven(object_inven_id)
4570: 					if object_inven then
4571: 						object, index = self:findInInventoryBy(
4572: 							object_inven, conditions[1], conditions[2])
4573: 					end
4574: 				else
4575: 					-- Can't use Actor:findInAllInventories() here;
4576: 					-- if a matching item is worn but there's also a
4577: 					-- matching item in the pack,
4578: 					-- findInAllInventories() may return the one that
4579: 					-- is in the pack instead of the worn one
4580: 					--
4581: 					-- So manually search only the worn inventories
4582: 					-- instead
4583: 					for inven_id, inven in pairs(self.inven) do
4584: 						if self:getInven(inven_id).worn then
4585: 							object, index = self:findInInventoryBy(inven, conditions[1], conditions[2])
4586: 							if object then
4587: 								object_inven_id = inven_id
4588: 								break
4589: 							end
4590: 						end
4591: 					end
4592: 				end
4593: 				-- If we're wearing it, add it to the list.
4594: 				if object and
4595: 					(not object.set_complete or not object.set_complete[set_id])
4596: 				then
4597: 					table.insert(set_objects, {
4598: 												 object = object,
4599: 												 index = index,
4600: 												 inven_id = object_inven_id,
4601: 												 data = conditions.data,})
4602: 				end
4603: 			end
4604: 			-- If we found all the objects.
4605: 			if #set_objects == #set_list then
4606: 				-- Add self to set objects.
4607: 				table.insert(set_objects, {
4608: 											 object = o,
4609: 											 inven_id = inven_id,
4610: 											 data = set_list.self_data,})
4611: 				-- Apply set bonuses.
4612: 				for _, d in pairs(set_objects) do
4613: 					if d.object ~= o then self:onTakeoff(d.object, d.inven_id, true) end
4614: 					local complete = d.object.on_set_complete
4615: 					if type(complete) == "table" then complete = complete[set_id] end
4616: 					if complete then complete(d.object, self, d.inven_id, set_objects) end
4617: 					if d.object ~= o then self:onWear(d.object, d.inven_id, true) end
4618: 						self:useObjectDisable(d.object)
4619: 						self:useObjectEnable(d.object)
4620: 
4621: 					d.object.set_complete = d.object.set_complete or {}
4622: 					d.object.set_complete[set_id] = set_objects
4623: 				end
4624: 			end
4625: 		end
4626: 	end

7601: 	-- check general status immunities
7602: 	--print("testing with effect", eid, e) table.print(e)

3060: 	end,

353: 		end

355: 		return true

95: 		m.ai_real = m.ai
96: 		m.ai = "summoned"
97: 	end

100: 	m.summoner_gain_exp = true
101: 	m.demonic_summon = true
102: 	m.dead = nil
103: 	m.dead_by_unsummon = nil
104: 	m:removeEffectsFilter(m, function() return true end, 9999, true, true)
105: 
106: 	m.life_regen = 0
107: 
108: 	m:setPersonalReaction(self, 100)
109: 	m.never_anger = 1
110: 	m.unused_stats = 0

113: 	m.unused_talents_types = 0

116: 	m.minion_be_nice = 1
117: 	m.from_doom_concordat = nil
118: 	m.save_hotkeys = true
119: 	m.ai_state = m.ai_state or {}
120: 	m.ai_state.tactic_leash = 100
121: 	m.ai_talents = self.stored_ai_talents and self.stored_ai_talents[m.name] or {}
122: 	if game.party:hasMember(self) then

131: 	-- m:resolve() m:resolve(nil, true)

145: 	end

148: -- Define the fields that are sync'ed online, and how they are sync'ed
149: profile_defs = {
150: 	allow_build = { {name="index:string:50"}, receive=function(data, save) save[data.name] = true end, export=function(env) for k, _ in pairs(env) do add{name=k} end end },
151: 	lore = { {name="index:string:30"}, receive=function(data, save) save.lore = save.lore or {} save.lore[data.name] = true end, export=function(env) for k, v in pairs(env.lore or {}) do add{name=k} end end },
152: 	escorts = { incr_only=true, {fate="index:enum(lost,betrayed,zigur,saved)"}, {nb="number"}, receive=function(data, save) inc_set(save, data.fate, data, "nb") end, export=function(env) for k, v in pairs(env) do add{fate=k, nb=v} end end },
153: 	artifacts = { incr_only=true, {cid="index:string:50"}, {name="index:string:40"}, {nb="number"}, receive=function(data, save) save.artifacts = save.artifacts or {} save.artifacts[data.cid] = save.artifacts[data.cid] or {} inc_set(save.artifacts[data.cid], data.name, data, "nb") end, export=function(env) for cid, d in pairs(env.artifacts or {}) do for name, v in pairs(d) do add{cid=cid, name=name, nb=v} end end end },
154: 	characters = { incr_only=true, {cid="index:string:50"}, {nb="number"}, receive=function(data, save) save.characters = save.characters or {} inc_set(save.characters, data.cid, data, "nb") end, export=function(env) for k, v in pairs(env.characters or {}) do add{cid=k, nb=v} end end },
155: 	uniques = { incr_only=true, {cid="index:string:50"}, {victim="index:string:50"}, {nb="number"}, receive=function(data, save) save.uniques = save.uniques or {} save.uniques[data.cid] = save.uniques[data.cid] or {} inc_set(save.uniques[data.cid], data.victim, data, "nb") end, export=function(env) for cid, d in pairs(env.uniques or {}) do for name, v in pairs(d) do add{cid=cid, victim=name, nb=v} end end end },
156: 	deaths = { incr_only=true, {cid="index:string:50"}, {source="index:string:50"}, {nb="number"}, receive=function(data, save) save.sources = save.sources or {} save.sources[data.cid] = save.sources[data.cid] or {} inc_set(save.sources[data.cid], data.source, data, "nb") end, export=function(env) for cid, d in pairs(env.sources or {}) do for name, v in pairs(d) do add{cid=cid, source=name, nb=v} end end end },
157: 	achievements = { {id="index:string:40"}, {gained_on="timestamp"}, {who="string:50"}, {turn="number"}, receive=function(data, save) save[data.id] = {who=data.who, when=data.gained_on, turn=data.turn} end, export=function(env) for id, v in pairs(env) do add{id=id, who=v.who, gained_on=v.when, turn=v.turn} end end },
158: 	donations = { no_sync=true, {last_ask="timestamp"}, receive=function(data, save) save.last_ask = data.last_ask end, export=function(env) add{last_ask=env.last_ask} end },
159: 	scores = {
160: 		no_sync=true,
161: 		receive=function(data,save)
162: 			save.sc = save.sc or {}
163: 			save.sc[data.world] = save.sc[data.world] or {}
164: 			save.sc[data.world].alive = save.sc[data.world].alive or {}
165: 			save.sc[data.world].dead = save.sc[data.world].dead or {}
166: 			if data.type == "alive" then
167: 				save.sc[data.world].alive = save.sc[data.world].alive or {}
168: 				save.sc[data.world].alive[data.name] = data
169: 			else
170: 				-- clear any 'alive' entry with this name
171: 				save.sc[data.world].alive[data.name] = nil
172: 				save.sc[data.world].dead = save.sc[data.world].dead or {}
173: 				save.sc[data.world].dead[#save.sc[data.world].dead+1] = data
174: 			end
175: 		end
176: 	},
177: }

108: 	id = "cults-godfeaster",
109: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
110: 	name = _t"between a rock and a soft place",
111: 	lore = _t[[You ever gotten yourself into a mess that you didn't know how to get out of? Well, that's kind of where I'm at right now. This thing, whatever it is, just burst out of the ground and swallowed me whole. Normally a girl has to get offered on an altar to monsters to get eaten like this, but it looks like this one just took a fancy to me.
112: 
113: I've seen a lot of things. Undead, horrors, sometimes a bear with psychic powers, but whatever this thing is, it's in a league of its own. It's like I'm inside a snake with the way it winds and how long it is. Sometimes these meaty bits of something come after me and have acid pouring out of them... I get the impression that it's trying to digest me. I've managed to make a little hideout in one of the folds of its belly, but I don't know how long these protective runes are going to last.
114: 
115: So, I guess my plan is to find a way out of here or to take this thing down with me. For most things, food goes in one end and... Well, you know the rest. But this thing... It just flat out digests everything it swallows. I've watched those things breaking down entire chunks of rock, houses, enough trees to fill a forest... This thing can eat pretty much everything.
116: 
117: With that in mind, my only option is to kill it from the inside. Dunno how I'm going to do that just yet.]],
118: }

131: 	lore = function() return ([[Being an adventurer is supposed to be fun. You know, get out there, kill a couple monsters, grab some loot, spend all the loot money you made and repeat. Most people who make puzzles like these usually leave some hints, but I've got nothing to work with!

173: newLore{
174: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-1",
175: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
176: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (1)",
177: 	lore = _t[[So, what does an adventurer do when they get bored with it all? For me, I wanted to find a nice castle somewhere out in the countryside and spend the rest of my days in idle contentment. The issue there is that I made a lot of enemies who would have loved for me to settle down in one spot, so I needed to think of a solution.
178: 
179: That's when I found this place. Everyone else avoided it because people never left once they went inside it. Being used to the adventuring life, I saw such a thing as a challenge. Turns out that this cursed castle, as people referred to it, constantly changes its inside layout. No one really knows how or why it does it, but I'm not really one to question such things. If I could just work out the logic behind how it shifted itself, I could have an unassailable fortress. 
180: 
181: However, I also found that this still didn't deter people from coming to kill me. They all swarmed in and although a lot of them got lost in the hallways, a few actually managed to reach me. I had grown rather attached to the place at this point, but neither could I stay there. My solution came with a bizarre tome I had found in my adventures. When I opened the cover and pointed it in the right direction, it could suck things into its very pages.
182: 
183: So, being the savvy adventurer I am, I opened the tome and sucked the entire castle inside of it. It seems like the tome could only suck so much inside its covers, so it could no longer hold anything else in it. Although I had to sacrifice a great treasure, I now had a sanctuary away from the real world which I could escape to whenever I needed shelter.]],
184: }

186: newLore{
187: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-2",
188: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
189: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (2)",
190: 	lore = _t[[As much as I love this castle, it really does give you a headache after a while. Whenever I tried to decorate rooms or organise anything in its interior, I would inevitably find the room in a completely different area. While I can navigate through the place without too much trouble now, it's still pretty annoying when I have to find a specific room.
191: 
192: I sometimes wonder if I'll ever run into the people who entered this place and never left. The shifting rooms themselves aren't that difficult to understand, once you find out the patterns behind their changes. If I could work out, then surely someone else had to as well, right? I do sometimes feel as if I'm not really alone in the castle, despite being the only person who can even reach this place, not to mention the only living thing walking these halls. I haven't seen so much as a mouse since I trapped the castle within my book.
193: 
194: I fear that I'm also starting to develop an unhealthy attachment to this place. I have not been able to have a single day of peace since I began my adventuring career, so the security these glass walls offer is becoming far too alluring to me.]],
195: }

201: 	lore = _t[[I knew it. I'm not alone in here. While I was right that I'm the only living thing, this castle does have its own guardians and servitors. Animated golems made of glass wander the halls now, searching for me. My fortress is no longer mine and there is no safety to be found within these walls. I knew that I could never truly find somewhere I could be safe, not in this book or in the outside world. I do not know where these golems came from. Perhaps the castle itself is trying to expel me from it or maybe I triggered some defence by wandering into the wrong room.
202: 
203: My treasure is stored somewhere in this castle, but I just don't care anymore. Escaping with my life will be treasure enough. When I reach the outside world again, maybe I'll drop the tome in a river and hope that no one else tries their luck with this place. I'm sure the spirits that haunt this place will rest easier knowing that there won't be any more victims.]],

110: 	display = '&', color_r=255, color_g=0, color_b=220, back_color=colors.VIOLET, image = "terrain/solidwall/solid_floor1.png",
111: 	notice = true,

114: 	desc = _t[[A farportal is a way to travel incredible distances in the blink of an eye. They were left behind by the powerful Sher'tul race.

119: 	checkSpecialLocation = function(self, who, q)
120: 		-- Caldizar space fortress
121: 		if rng.percent(5) and not game.state:hasSeenSpecialFarportal("caldizar-space-fortress") then
122: 			game:changeLevel(1, "shertul-fortress-caldizar", {direct_switch=true})
123: 			q:exploratory_energy()
124: 			game.log("#VIOLET#You enter the swirling portal and in the blink of an eye you set foot in a strangely familiar zone, right next to a farportal...")
125: 			game.state:seenSpecialFarportal("caldizar-space-fortress")
126: 			return true
127: 		end
128: 		-- Eidolon plane, for RL characters only
129: 		if rng.percent(10) and not game.state:hasSeenSpecialFarportal("eidolon") and not who.easy_mode_lifes and not who.infinite_lifes then
130: 			local zone = game.party:goToEidolon()
131: 			zone.from_farportal = true
132: 			q:exploratory_energy()
133: 			game.log("#VIOLET#You enter the swirling portal and in the blink of an eye you set foot in strange empty space...")
134: 			game.state:seenSpecialFarportal("eidolon")
135: 			return true
136: 		end
137: 		if self:triggerHook{"ShertulFortress:exploratoryPortal:specialLocation", q=q, who=who} then
138: 			return true
139: 		end
140: 	end,
141: 
142: 	on_move = function(self, x, y, who)
143: 		if not who.player then return end
144: 		local Dialog = require "engine.ui.Dialog"
145: 		local q = who:hasQuest("shertul-fortress")
146: 		if not q then Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Exploratory Farportal", _t"The farportal seems to be inactive") return end
147: 		if q:isCompleted("farportal-broken") then Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Exploratory Farportal", _t"The farportal is broken and will not be usable anymore.") return end
148: 		if not q:exploratory_energy(true) then Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Exploratory Farportal", _t"The fortress does not have enough energy to power a trip through the portal.") return end
149: 
150: 		Dialog:yesnoPopup(_t"Exploratory Farportal", _t"Do you want to travel in the farportal? You cannot know where you will end up.", function(ret) if ret then
151: 			if not game:changeLevelCheck(1, {}, {direct_switch=true}) then return end
152: 			if self:checkSpecialLocation(who, q) then return end
153: 
154: 			local zone, boss = game.state:createRandomZone()
155: 			zone.no_worldport = true
156: 			zone.force_farportal_recall = true
157: 			zone.generator.actor.abord_no_guardian = true
158: 			zone.objects_cost_modifier = 0.1
159: 			zone.make_back_portal = function(self)
160: 				local p = game:getPlayer(true)
161: 				local x, y = p.x, p.y
162: 				local g = game.zone:makeEntityByName(game.level, "terrain", game.zone.basic_floor)
163: 				if g.change_level then return end
164: 				g = g:clone()
165: 				g:removeAllMOs(true)
166: 				g:altered()
167: 				g.show_tooltip = true
168: 				g.name = _t"Exploratory Farportal exit"
169: 				g.display = '&' g.color_r = colors.VIOLET.r g.color_g = colors.VIOLET.g g.color_b = colors.VIOLET.b
170: 				g.add_displays = g.add_displays or {}
171: 				g.add_displays[#g.add_displays+1] = mod.class.Grid.new{image="terrain/maze_teleport.png"}
172: 				g.notice = true
173: 				g.change_level = 1 g.change_zone = "shertul-fortress"
174: 				game.zone:addEntity(game.level, g, "terrain", x, y)
175: 				if self then game.logSeen(self, "#VIOLET#As %s falls you notice a portal appearing.", self:getName())
176: 				else game.logSeen(p, "#VIOLET#Your rod of recall shakes, a portal appears beneath you.") end

698: newLore{
699: 	id = "kestin-highfin-adventuring-notes",
700: 	category = "highfin",
701: 	name = _t"On Adventuring",
702: 	lore = _t[[I must say, as time grows, I feel so do I grow more and more inclined to distance myself from the calling of an 'adventurer', like so many you can find roaming the countryside. I feel like the myth of a wandering hero has blinded too many with promise of easy fame and riches, with no eye for the other kind of fortune.
703: 
704: Hear me out on this.
705: 
706: Nowadays most don't really recognize how fascinating the world we live in truly is. It is vast, more than you can imagine. I can safely promise, any wild thought you can muster up, dear reader, will not come close to the truth. Such is the breadth of wonders, I would probably dismiss most of what I have seen as myth, be I not there myself. And even then sometimes, I had to wonder whether I could trust my eyes.
707: 
708: Perhaps I'm being too vague, or maybe these promises leave much to be desired. After all, adventuring is not all fun and exotics, it is before all danger and a constant threat of death, or worse. So then if you wish me to be more concrete, think of derelict, crumbling crypts, cults and demons, hungry forests full of monsters and forces beyond time and place. True, there is overwhelming awe, thrill even, but the reason that so little detail reaches you, is because so little live to tell.
709: 
710: What does reach us then, are not people, but objects. Artifacts of great power, legacy of the past. Surely, any drunkard might like to tell tales after a pint or two, but a magical sword is a proof of its own and it keeps quiet of what it has seen. So, a great hero is usually easy to recognize, being practically a walking history book. Clad in half the age of important events which he probably has no idea about.
711: 
712: It is important to remember, that every artifact has a meaning, beings of great power and importance behind them. Stories, that now slowly wane into nothing. This is why it is not artifacts that make an adventurer. It is his great deeds, the will to dare where nobody did before. It is not important if you get known in the process or not, after all, if you were truly great, maybe you will leave behind a legacy of your own.
713: 
714: -#{italic}#Kestin Highfin#{normal}#]]
715: }

717: newLore{
718: 	id = "galsame-orientation-notes",
719: 	category = "point zero",
720: 	name = _t"Warden-Master Galsamae's Orientation Notes",
721: 	lore = _t[[Congratulations, sir and/or madam. Whether by invitation, discovering it on your own, or simply being enough of a thorn in our side to recruit rather than dispose of, you have gained the secrets of chronomancy. The ultimate power of time - the ability to reset and try again if you fail, the ability to save time by seeing the results of investigations before they happen. Though our powers are bound to post-Spellblaze Eyal, they are those of nigh-omnipotence with enough patience.
722: 
723: But trust me - "enough patience" is one nasty limiting reagent. You're going to be running out of that fast when you've spent the last week trying to dismantle an Age of Dusk-era house-of-cards system of causally interdependent tyrannies without causing dwarven extinction, and a plague just broke out right when you had things almost perfect, for the sixth time--
724: 
725: Look. The point is, there's a reason the person who writes the invitations and the mission statements isn't someone out in the field - and you're lucky enough to be working for someone who understands that you need more flexibility than idealism allows. Our squad knows that to stay sane, we have to know when "time flows forward at a rate of one second per second" isn't the only rule we have to break. That it's generally okay to skip the trial and just deal with a temporally hazardous jackass as you see fit, if you've foreseen a guilty verdict - as long as your investigations are solid when you actually conduct them (and you do have to do the work once in a while, or you'll only be capable of seeing yourself procrastinating). And if you just need to not be watched, you should know that there are a few decades in the Age of Dusk we and a few other squads recognize as "fair game" - whatever experiments you've wondered about or horrors you want to inflict, just keep it to the time period of infinite forgotten evils and it doesn't hurt anything in the grand scheme. Trust me, we've checked - nothing in that time period matters unless you've got another Spellblaze to set off.
726: 
727: But most importantly, you should know: Zemekkys is even lazier than I am, but he has status to maintain. If you continually violate his will, there will come a point at which you will be informed that you have been caught and should stop resisting. Accept whatever fate he doles out for you. If you do not stop, there will come a point where he will be forced to make an example of you so severe that the entire cosmos will notice your non-existence. Obviously we can't be sure how many of us he's done this to (if any) or how it works, but we're pretty sure that the result looks like something starting with a W.
728: 
729: Everyone here wants the same thing - keep spacetime stable, have fun with your powers, cheat at a few lotteries - but we've got cover to maintain and, in theory, an actual job to do if something ever cracks that Sher'Tul shield or the Greigu find a way to bypass a portal-filter. Scratch backs when yours gets scratched, don't make so much noise that the system comes crashing down on your head, and you'll enjoy your stay in eternity.
730: 
731: Welcome to Point Zero, agent. Enclosed are timespace coordinates to what is, quite literally, the best roast-yeti restaurant that could possibly exist - I'll have the squad meet you there and then. Thank me later.
732: 
733: [i]-Galsamae[/i]
734: 
735: PS: You might encounter a... benefactor of sorts in your travels. You'll know it when you see it, ham-fistedly yanking its puppets back from the brink of death; if you see it for yourself, we regret to inform you that you've taken a one-way trip off prime Timeline-E4-RL territory for a doomed offshoot unless "he" feels like weaving you back in - and it tends to only do that to people who narrowly avert its engineered apocalypses through incredible power or luck. If you have been chosen by its schemes, play along and you might get brought back from the temporal graveyard that is the Timeline-E4-EXPADV subnetwork. We do not know what it is - a runaway creation of our own, a competing culture's weapon, or something far above ourselves - but if it has hostile intent, it has already won. So far it's been... mostly cooperative. Just make a point not to remind it that we're its competition.]]
736: }

150: 	lore = _t[[Thought is treasure. Treasure thoughts. Spin fates, tell tales, words of gods, smith into fables. All that is can be rewritten and all writing is defined by what is. Cascades upon cascades which blend into reality, ever altering, ever changing, ever being, ever ceasing.
151: 
152: Words are power. My power is words. I am infinity and its end. Everything is possible.]],

173: newLore{
174: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-1",
175: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
176: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (1)",
177: 	lore = _t[[So, what does an adventurer do when they get bored with it all? For me, I wanted to find a nice castle somewhere out in the countryside and spend the rest of my days in idle contentment. The issue there is that I made a lot of enemies who would have loved for me to settle down in one spot, so I needed to think of a solution.
178: 
179: That's when I found this place. Everyone else avoided it because people never left once they went inside it. Being used to the adventuring life, I saw such a thing as a challenge. Turns out that this cursed castle, as people referred to it, constantly changes its inside layout. No one really knows how or why it does it, but I'm not really one to question such things. If I could just work out the logic behind how it shifted itself, I could have an unassailable fortress. 
180: 
181: However, I also found that this still didn't deter people from coming to kill me. They all swarmed in and although a lot of them got lost in the hallways, a few actually managed to reach me. I had grown rather attached to the place at this point, but neither could I stay there. My solution came with a bizarre tome I had found in my adventures. When I opened the cover and pointed it in the right direction, it could suck things into its very pages.
182: 
183: So, being the savvy adventurer I am, I opened the tome and sucked the entire castle inside of it. It seems like the tome could only suck so much inside its covers, so it could no longer hold anything else in it. Although I had to sacrifice a great treasure, I now had a sanctuary away from the real world which I could escape to whenever I needed shelter.]],
184: }

186: newLore{
187: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-2",
188: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
189: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (2)",
190: 	lore = _t[[As much as I love this castle, it really does give you a headache after a while. Whenever I tried to decorate rooms or organise anything in its interior, I would inevitably find the room in a completely different area. While I can navigate through the place without too much trouble now, it's still pretty annoying when I have to find a specific room.
191: 
192: I sometimes wonder if I'll ever run into the people who entered this place and never left. The shifting rooms themselves aren't that difficult to understand, once you find out the patterns behind their changes. If I could work out, then surely someone else had to as well, right? I do sometimes feel as if I'm not really alone in the castle, despite being the only person who can even reach this place, not to mention the only living thing walking these halls. I haven't seen so much as a mouse since I trapped the castle within my book.
193: 
194: I fear that I'm also starting to develop an unhealthy attachment to this place. I have not been able to have a single day of peace since I began my adventuring career, so the security these glass walls offer is becoming far too alluring to me.]],
195: }

197: newLore{
198: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-3",
199: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
200: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (3)",
201: 	lore = _t[[I knew it. I'm not alone in here. While I was right that I'm the only living thing, this castle does have its own guardians and servitors. Animated golems made of glass wander the halls now, searching for me. My fortress is no longer mine and there is no safety to be found within these walls. I knew that I could never truly find somewhere I could be safe, not in this book or in the outside world. I do not know where these golems came from. Perhaps the castle itself is trying to expel me from it or maybe I triggered some defence by wandering into the wrong room.

468: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-general_of_urh_rok",
469: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
470: 	name = _t"demon statue: Khulmanar, General of Urh'Rok",
471: 	lore = _t[=[Our tournaments, run ever since our salvation from the dust mages under the command and inspiration of Urh'Rok, are not simply tests of direct combat, as many may think.  We have those, yes, but we also have competitions for scholarly work, attentiveness, physical endurance, philosophy, and countless other fields.  Perhaps the most prestigious of these, though, is the Divine Tournament of Tactics, by which our military leaders are selected.  Through a series of trials, we are compared in our abilities to assess a combat scenario and swiftly handle it, rated on speed, casualties, deployment efficiency, and a variety of other factors.  Khulmanar, a child of onyx, is the reigning champion of these, and has been for most of the time that we've spent waiting for our continent to reach Eyal.  Chosen by our process as the wisest tactical mind among our people, he was selected to meet with Urh'Rok himself to gain his approval to lead our forces in the invasion.  Urh'Rok was so impressed by Khulmanar that he used a significant portion of the little energy he's not using to hold our world together to build Khulmanar a new body, one strong enough to let him direct battles from the front-line without fear.  With a form and weapons granted by our Father, and a mind given his direct, enthusiastic approval, Khulmanar is considered to be the avatar of Urh'Rok, and his commands in battle are to be treated with the same reverence we would give to the words of Father himself.]=]
472: }

474: newLore{

476: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
477: 	name = _t"demon statue: Lithfengel",
478: 	lore = _t[=[Lithfengel, mentor of Draebor and child of emerald, was one of our finest scholars.  When most of us were still too afraid to go near a portal, he recovered an intact one and began to pry apart its secrets, in hopes of reaching Eyal.  His data showed that although this portal was still technically connected to Eyal, the link between the two worlds was still fluctuating far too much to make it safe for travel, the still-raging flames threatening to tear any prospective passengers apart before they reached their destination.  Rather than try to repair the link directly, he went into his lab and didn't emerge for a few days; when he came out, he glowed with a strange new enchantment, proclaiming it would adaptively mutate him to endure whatever damage the portal would otherwise inflict.  Saying that the consequences of failure were too awful to risk inflicting on other test subjects, he entered the portal himself, promising to return immediately after he arrived; he has not been seen since.  May he rest in peace for his selfless devotion.]=]
479: }

482: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-rogroth",
483: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
484: 	name = _t"demon statue: Rogroth, Eater of Souls",
485: 	lore = _t[=[Recently, the cultists of Shasshhiy'Kaish have begun speaking of a "demon seed," a sort of magical cluster of life-essence which can be implanted in a sentient being, allowing it to grow inside of them and eventually become one of our citizens.  Inspired by this idea, the children of emerald have developed a prototype of this form of magic, and the children of onyx have made a chassis to carry it into combat.  Rogroth generates countless essence-less seeds from within its frame, then embeds them in nearby living beings, so when they expire, their life-essence goes directly into the seed and allows it to grow.  We have not yet perfected its production capabilities, so currently the seeds will only become degenerate husks when they grow, but fear not!  As we get data from the tests of this design, we'll improve on it, and soon the slaughter of our foes will cause wretchlings, quasits, and even thaurheregs to spring up from their corpses.  With a little bit of luck and some decisive early skirmishes, we could even bypass the problem of getting an invasion force to the surface entirely, growing it there instead.]=]
486: }

489: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-corrupted_daelach",
490: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
491: 	name = _t"demon statue: Corrupted Daelach",
492: 	lore = _t[=[One of the problems with making daelach is the inherent instability that comes from creating something that is almost entirely made of magic.  If ambient levels of blight are even slightly too high, it can set off a chain reaction that at best destroys the daelach, and at worst destroys most of the mages who were building it.  Daelach production is thus theoretically cheap, but in practice involves great expense, and usually a blighted daelach has to be immediately put down lest it cause tremendous damage.  One specimen, though, adapted to the blight in a very interesting way, sprouting wings and bolstering its usual firestorms with blight, but otherwise remaining perfectly balanced and controllable.  We'll try to recreate this happy accident however we can, but in the meantime, it will prove effective on the surface of Eyal.]=]
493: }

496: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-harkor_zun",
497: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
498: 	name = _t"demon statue: Harkor'Zun",
499: 	lore = _t[=[Of the anomalies and phenomena we've noticed in our studies of the shield protecting Eyal, none have frustrated us so much as meteors.  Certain powerful Eyalite spellcasters can pull a large meteor into low orbit, passing it through the shield relatively unharmed, aside from being split into predictably-sized chunks, which are then called to the surface one-by-one in a series of devastating meteoric crashes.  While we have not yet found a way to reverse-engineer these spells to protect our standard troops from disintegration, we have had some limited success in making a construct that closely resembles a meteor in composition and appearance.  Harkor'Zun, a being made mostly of stone, was simply dropped from our platform; the shield shattered him as expected, but we had designed him to survive this, the fragments merging back into their completed form once he reached the surface.  It would seem, though, that either we made him to be too sturdy, or the shield envelops incoming objects in a sort of anti-magic coating, as he has been unable to start the second stage of this process, wherein he merges these fragments back into a completed form.  Should an Eyalite stumble upon him and attempt to destroy the fragments, Harkor'Zun will be able to re-combine and "thank" whoever granted him his ascension.]=]
500: }

135: "It's your lucky day, <?=player.name?>," your handler says as he leads you to a large, glowing crystal.  "You're too cooperative to stay in testing any longer.  Today, you're getting promoted to research assistant!"  You're nearly beside yourself with joy!  "Now, we'll need to do a short little process first.  Fireproofing wards here, loyalty reinforcement there, standard-issue alteration, but mostly just linking your consciousness to this," he says, pointing to the crystal.  "With this thing, everything you see, hear, smell, taste, or feel gets fed directly into this little ol' beauty.  Not just that, either - whereever you go, and whatever you think, we'll have it saved for future reference."  You're going to help them learn so much!  "Just step on the plate here, and hold your arms like this so I can get the bindings in place..."
136: 
137: That crystal.  That crystal is how they're keeping track of you, and it has most of what you helped them discover trapped within it.  If you break it, you'll be able to escape their notice for the first time since you arrived here, allowing you to get away without them finding you again, and as an added bonus you'll undo most of what you helped them accomplish.  You need to destroy it, then flee for your life!]=]
